cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We filled it over ten years. I shouldn't have to decide alone what survives us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. Taking it away can't mean you inherit all the deciding.

mechanism: A authorizes postponement and custody of letters only with a jointly scheduled decision, sharing emotional labor without surrendering it to one person.
confusable: D81 seeks acknowledgment of history; D77 seeks shared participation in the difficult present task it leaves.
comparison: A former couple sorting letters differs from siblings dividing care paperwork.
seedUse: Use D77-b offered box custody and inability to read today; preserve the insistence that neither inherits deciding alone.
